PullRequest.Title: chat: Move browse actions to customization headers
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

Moves the marketplace **Browse** actions on the Plugins, MCP Servers, and Skills pages into the top-right page header, matching the Browse page's **Add Customization** placement. On the Plugins page, **Configure Marketplaces** is available from an adjacent ellipsis overflow menu. These controls remain visible only while marketplace discovery is available.

- `npm run stylelint -- src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\browser\aiCustomization\media\aiCustomizationManagement.css` — passed
- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` — passed
- `npm run build-fast` — passed
- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed
- `.\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\aiCustomization\pluginListWidget.test.ts --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\aiCustomization\mcpListWidget.test.ts` — 130 passing
- Manual Code OSS validation — Plugins, MCP Servers, and Skills each show **Browse** in the top-right header; the Plugins ellipsis control matches the Browse button height and opens **Configure Marketplaces**; activating it opens the existing **Manage Plugin Marketplaces** quick pick; disabling Marketplace hides the entry points

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening the AI customization management editor constructs the Skills, MCP Servers, and Plugins widgets and their new persistent header controls.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The diff adds one Button for Skills, one for MCP Servers, and two for Plugins during synchronous widget DOM construction. Visibility is computed from in-memory configuration/source metadata; existing asynchronous model/provider refreshes remain outside the changed header work and were already launched by these widget constructors.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Conditionally loads the existing MCP gallery snapshot after widget construction.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most the existing snapshot request when its visibility/state guards permit it; no request is caused by creating or hiding the new button.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The MCP widget constructor already called refresh before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asynchronous existing population work, not required for the new header control to render.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing plugin/provider item refresh during widget initialization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing initial refresh per widget instance, with provider work determined by the active harness.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The Plugins widget already performed the same initial refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asynchronous list population; the new buttons add no wait or call.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed number of widgets/buttons per editor instance; availability checks scan the small configured marketplace-source list rather than installed items.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No concurrency is introduced by header construction. Existing widget refreshes may overlap across independently constructed widgets exactly as before.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Header availability is recomputed from current in-memory source metadata. Existing MCP/plugin snapshots and item-model state retain their prior cold/warm behavior; the diff neither invalidates nor bypasses them.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: constructor and helper call paths show only fixed DOM allocation plus an in-memory source filter on changed lines.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Button construction cost is not measured, but it is fixed and tiny; no input-dependent or boundary cost was added.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The fixed eager allocation is bounded, while moving Browse out of group renderers removes repeated per-render button allocation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Switching customization sections or changing marketplace configuration/source availability updates header visibility and refreshes the active lists.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A section switch performs a style.display update before the existing item-model load. Relevant configuration/source events perform the same in-memory visibility update immediately, then follow the pre-existing filter/refresh paths.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing marketplace query when already browsing/searching; otherwise refresh filters in-memory/plugin-provider state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most the same logical refresh per relevant source/configuration event as before; the added updateHeaderActions does not add another refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same configuration and onDidChangeSources handlers already called refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing asynchronous results population after the immediate visibility update.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing guarded MCP gallery snapshot query.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Same guarded snapshot query count as before; cancellation/snapshot state prevent stale work.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same handlers already refreshed MCP data.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing asynchronous list population, not part of the style update itself.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing item-model section loading may discover customization files/providers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing model section load per user section selection, with observable/model reuse determining warm behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Section selection already loaded the same item model before the header action moved.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The returned setSection promise already waits for this load; updateHeaderActions adds no boundary or await.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One visibility check per relevant event, linear only in the small marketplace-source metadata list; section switches are user-driven. Existing list work scales with installed/catalog items independently of the new check.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Plugin and MCP requests retain their existing cancellation tokens and snapshot guards; the added visibility update is synchronous and does not schedule parallel work. ResizeObserver relayout can occur after a genuine header-height change and is browser-coalesced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The new check has no cache but only filters source metadata. Plugin/MCP snapshots, request cancellation, and item-model observables are unchanged; cold refreshes and warm renders behave as before.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed handlers add only updateHeaderActions before unchanged refresh/filter calls, and availability is an in-memory configuration/source filter.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact relayout duration depends on editor width and wrapping, but changes occur only on user section switches or rare source/configuration changes and no collection-wide work was placed in the observer.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added synchronous work is bounded and rare, and all expensive refresh boundaries retain their previous cardinality and scheduling.

Scenarios.Scenario: Clicking Browse from the Skills, MCP Servers, or Plugins header navigates to the marketplace discovery page and loads catalog results.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The moved button fires the same existing onDidRequestBrowse event; the editor selects the corresponding marketplace section, whose discovery page performs the catalog query. The button relocation adds no extra await or query.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Queries enabled marketplace providers for the selected customization type/source.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One query per enabled source for a page, concurrently; pagination/backfill remains bounded by existing page limits.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The removed per-group Browse buttons fired the same event and reached the identical discovery-page query path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Catalog results wait for the provider page, as before.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One logical catalog load per click. Effective network cardinality is one provider query per enabled source, concurrently, with page size bounds and optional bounded filtered backfill.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: CustomizationMarketplaceService uses Promise.all across enabled sources for a page; the discovery page cancels the prior request before starting another. This concurrency and cancellation behavior are unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Continuation state is retained in a bounded LRU and subsequent pagination uses cursors; changing selection cancels prior work. Cold and warm behavior are unchanged because the same event and discovery page are reached.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: old and new button handlers both fire the same emitter, and traced listeners select the same discovery section.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider latency and enabled-source count vary by environment, but the PR does not change either count or scheduling.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; this is a relocation of the trigger with identical boundary fan-out, caching, and cancellation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening the new Plugins overflow menu and choosing Configure Marketplaces runs the existing marketplace-management command.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Opening the context menu allocates one Action/DisposableStore in memory. Only explicitly selecting Configure Marketplaces invokes the command; the quick pick initially reads configuration, and later user choices may perform a filesystem existence check or provider management operation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Checks whether the selected marketplace repository URI exists before presenting follow-up actions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One filesystem existence check after the user selects one configured marketplace.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Plugins home had no adjacent overflow entry, although the same command and boundary were already available from the command palette and discovery-page source menu.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks only that explicit follow-up quick pick, not editor startup, menu opening, or list rendering.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Delegates to an active harness marketplace-management provider when present.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider workflow per explicit Configure Marketplaces selection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same command/provider workflow was reachable through existing surfaces, but this PR adds the Plugins-header entry point.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: User-initiated management workflow only; no work runs when the header renders or the overflow merely opens.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One action and menu per click. Configured marketplace rows scale with the configured reference count; filesystem existence is checked only for the single marketplace selected by the user, not for every row.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The quick-pick workflow is sequential and user-driven. Context-menu actions are disposed on hide; no burst or background loop is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Configuration is read fresh per command invocation; there is no new retained cache. Context-menu allocations are released by onHide.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed callback invokes the existing command only on Action.run, and the DisposableStore is released by context-menu onHide.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider implementations can vary, but invocation is explicit, singular, and off all startup/render/configuration critical paths.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The newly reachable work is bounded, intentional, user-triggered, and properly cleaned up.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all four changed files and traced editor construction, section/configuration updates, Browse navigation, catalog fan-out, and the new marketplace overflow command. The PR adds only fixed persistent controls and in-memory visibility checks, preserves existing network/filesystem cardinality on Browse and refresh paths, and disposes menu actions on hide. No high-confidence actionable performance regression or evidenced shipped-regression fix was found.
